RVA-F-0183.question: Which exact path changes city current production item +0x38 during a natural production-list session, and does its local command case validate the item ID?

scope.boundary: This packet distinguishes the observed command-five city item write from a bounded temporary cost-preview substitution. It classifies only command-five's local owner gate and write, not its submitting producer, UI commitment, general valid-ID rule, unsupported-ID behavior, or final production effects.

dependencies.use: Provides the five-word command record, dispatcher, 0-through-65 type table, and local queue path.
Establishes city +0x38 as the current item read by city update.
The earlier decoded displacement scan excluded indexed stores and prepared the runtime discriminator.
Binds observed IDs 101, 104, and 105 to initialized building identities.
Binds observed wonder item 218 to its initialized identity.

staticCommandCase.recordInput: 0x82CDDF18 through 0x82CDDF24 load record words +0x00 type into r30, +0x04 into r31, +0x08 into r15, and +0x0C into r29. The accepted 0-through-65 dispatch at 0x82CDDFF4 through 0x82CDE010 selects the case-five branch at 0x82CDFFF8.
staticCommandCase.ownerGate: 0x82CDFFFC through 0x82CE0010 form city 0x8314FE28 + 0xBC*r15, read signed owner byte +0x00, compare it with r31, and branch away when unequal.
staticCommandCase.writer: On the owner-matched path, 0x82CE0018 calls 0x82CB3F08 with r3=r15; the following 0x82CE001C forms city +0x38 and 0x82CE0020 stores the low halfword of unchanged record word +0x0C (r29). The helper return is not tested between the call and store.
staticCommandCase.localValidity: The case-five entry-to-store path does not compare r29 with an item-ID minimum, maximum, initialized record count, or definition presence. This is absence of a local check only; producer validation and behavior for unsupported IDs remain unresolved.

previewDistinction.writer: In 0x82CE9490, 0x82CE9DF8 saves city current item and 0x82CE9DFC temporarily stores a candidate building item. It calls BuildingWonderProductionCostLookup at 0x82CE9E00 and another helper at 0x82CE9E18, then 0x82CE9E20 restores the saved item. These two stores are not evidence that the candidate was committed as city production.
previewDistinction.qualification: The later output of the second helper and full list rendering are outside this packet.

runtimeObservation.session: One isolated interactive Title launch exited normally with code zero. The owner reported selecting buildings in sequence, beginning with Barracks and later Library. The default-off temporary write observer was enabled only for this launch. Its eight-event cap was reached; the build passed CTest with 41 passed and one skipped.
runtimeObservation.placement: Observed changed halfword writes to 0x8314FE60 + 0xBC*cityIndex for indices 0 through 63 when the new item was in 100 through 236; each event retained source file and line, city owner, old/new values, r3 through r6, and LR.
runtimeObservation.temporaryEvents: The other six captured changed-value events map to 0x82CE9DFC or 0x82CE9E20 in 0x82CE9490. They include candidate IDs 101, 104, and 105 but do not independently prove a lasting choice.
runtimeObservation.qualification: The session proves that command-five's city item store executed for IDs 101 and 104 during the interaction. It does not prove which item the user finally selected or that either item completed construction.

wonderSelectionFollowup.session: One owner-operated interactive scratch Title launch exited normally with code zero after the owner selected Manhattan Project. The default-off one-event observer was enabled for this launch.
wonderSelectionFollowup.placement: The observer ran immediately before the halfword store at 0x82CE0020 in 0x82CDDF08 and emitted exactly one owner-matched changed city +0x38 write for wonder item 218.
wonderSelectionFollowup.qualification: The observed store records the selected item write. The producer that submitted command five, construction completion, wonder effects, and behavior for other IDs were not observed.

minimalTitleProbe.status: Executed once; one matching wonder write was observed and is recorded under wonderSelectionFollowup.
minimalTitleProbe.placement: Default-off read-only observer at the exact guest store 0x82CE0020 in 0x82CDDF08. Emit only when the owner-matched city +0x38 changes to a wonder item ID from 200 through 232. Do not count preview substitutions at 0x82CE9DFC or 0x82CE9E20.
minimalTitleProbe.fields: City index and owner, old and new city +0x38 item IDs, guest store address and source function, and LR.
minimalTitleProbe.stop: Cap at one matching changed-value event. After selecting one wonder actually offered by the city list, exit normally. If no matching write occurs, report zero events and stop. This observes the selected item write only, not construction completion or effect execution.

currentEvidence.method: An approved interactive scratch-Title observer logged at most eight changed city +0x38 halfword writes, then a separate default-off one-event observer recorded a wonder choice at the same store. Both Title launches exited normally. Exact generated source lines identified two guest functions; a foreground read-only canonical-project raw-word query corroborated dispatcher inputs, type dispatch, owner gate, command store, and temporary preview/restore stores.

entries.result: Record type and three arguments are loaded and numeric case five selects the city write path.
An owner-matched city receives low halfword of record +0x0C at city +0x38; runtime observed building IDs 101 and 104 and wonder ID 218 at 0x82CE0020.
A candidate item is temporarily written, passed through the cost helper path, and the prior item is restored.

currentEvidence.qualification: The observed source-line-to-guest-store mapping is corroborated by current-image words. The wonder follow-up establishes one selected item ID only; neither session observed construction completion or effects. Private raw logs and temporary executables are not tracked evidence payloads.

guards: Do not call numeric type five the original platform command name without an independent source.
Do not treat the temporary candidate store as a lasting production selection.
Do not infer a global valid-ID rule from the local case-five absence of an ID check.
Do not infer construction or described building effects from the current-item write.
RVA-F-0183.conclusion: An observed numeric command-five path stores its record +0x0C low halfword to the owner-matched city's current production item +0x38 at 0x82CE0020. Runtime observed building IDs 101 and 104, plus selected wonder ID 218 (Manhattan Project), at that store. This local case has no item-ID validity check. A separate helper temporarily substitutes candidate IDs for a cost lookup and restores the prior item. The producer coverage, global validity rule, construction completion, and implemented effects remain unresolved.

RVA-F-0184.question: Which bounded producer supplies command type five's city item, and why can a city choice bypass the observed network submit entry?

scope.boundary: This packet follows three direct UI calls and the complete type-five record construction in one producer. It does not prove the UI list's valid-entry rule, the producer's runtime branch for the reported Barracks selection, unsupported-ID behavior, or construction effects.

dependencies.use: Provides the observed case-five city current-item write and temporary preview distinction.
Provides the five-word command record, local drain, and dispatcher.
Binds item 101 to the initialized Barracks definition.

choiceHandler.selectionReads: At 0x82E02D14 and 0x82E02D1C, 0x82E02CE0 reads selected value +0x448 and category +0x440 from its child object at parent +0xC40. A selected value of -1 enters a separate path before the three direct type-five calls.
choiceHandler.arguments: Each call passes the signed owner byte at city pointer +0x00 as r3, parent +0xC20 as r4, and the selected +0x448 value as r5. The handler also reads the city's prior item +0x38 for later display work. No item-domain bound or definition-presence test appears between the category branch and these calls; the list that supplies +0x448 remains unclassified.
choiceHandler.selectionChangeHelper: The call at 0x82E02D40 to 0x82E02C50 runs only when the selection changes. Its 0/1/2 category paths return without converting the selected value; its other-category paths do not establish building or wonder validity.

commandProducer.entry: 0x82CEE650 copies r3 to r31 (player), r4 to r30 (city), and r5 to r29 (selected item).
commandProducer.record: At 0x82CEE6BC through 0x82CEE6D0, stack +0x50 receives literal type 5, +0x54 receives player, +0x58 city, +0x5C item, and +0x60 receives the word at 0x82F7AD00. The item is forwarded without a local ID-range or definition-presence test.
commandProducer.route: A guarded branch constructs a command object with 0x82D90A18 and invokes a manager-child virtual slot. The other branch passes the stack record to local drain 0x82CE16C8 at 0x82CEE76C, which reaches dispatcher 0x82CDDF08 at 0x82CE17B0. The runtime branch taken by the reported Barracks selection was not observed directly.
commandProducer.qualification: The global fifth word, routing flags, and full UI-list population policy are unresolved. This producer is distinct from 0x82CE1950.

runtimeObservation.placement: A temporary default-off midasm hook at 0x82CE1950 logged only incoming type 5, LR, and r4 through r6, with an eight-event cap when REREVVED_CITY_ITEM_SUBMIT_PROBE=1. Generated code placed it before the entry instruction. The scratch Title build passed CTest with 41 passed and one skipped.
runtimeObservation.result: One isolated interactive session exited normally with code zero. The owner reported selecting Barracks. The enabled probe logged zero type-five calls at 0x82CE1950. This excludes observed use of that entry for type five in this session; it does not by itself prove the local producer branch executed or identify every command producer.
runtimeObservation.restoration: The two temporary scratch Title source files were restored byte-for-byte, the uninstrumented executable was rebuilt, and scratch Title Git state was clean. Canonical Title and SDK were unchanged.

currentEvidence.method: One approved bounded runtime submit-entry observation, followed by foreground read-only Ghidra raw-call, function, and exact-word queries against the pinned image. Generated-code inspection was restricted to the exact 0x82CEE650 and 0x82E02CE0 functions and three prior exact callsite windows.

entries.result: The non-truncated direct-caller scan found exactly these three static calls to 0x82CEE650; category 1 is the building branch.
Exact words store type 5 and the three forwarded arguments into consecutive command-record words.
The local branch passes the stack record to 0x82CE16C8; a non-truncated raw caller scan found the drain's one direct dispatcher call at 0x82CE17B0.
Zero type-five entry observations in the owner-reported Barracks-selection session.

currentEvidence.qualification: The configured Ghidra listing truncates 0x82CEE650 at its thunk, so exact raw words and narrow generated-code dataflow support its interior. The UI handler decompilation has a bad-instruction warning; exact callsites and field words corroborate the reported branch.

guards: Do not treat a selected UI value as validated merely because it reached the command producer.
Do not infer that every city choice bypasses 0x82CE1950 from one zero-event session.
Do not infer building completion or stored-description effects from a production-item command.
RVA-F-0184.conclusion: The city production UI has three direct calls to a distinct type-five producer for unit, building, and wonder choices. The producer forwards the selected item unchanged and can send its five-word record through the local drain to the observed city-item writer. The owner-reported Barracks session did not enter 0x82CE1950 with type five. The UI list's valid-entry rule and the exact runtime routing branch remain unresolved.

RVA-F-0185.question: Where does the production-choice child get selected item IDs, and what wonder IDs can this UI path enumerate?

scope.boundary: This packet establishes the production-choice child, its option-vector path, the local wonder enumeration bound, and the initialized building-list bound. It does not establish a global validity rule, all building-list predicates, runtime list contents, or the availability of other choice paths.

dependencies.use: Provides the child +0x440 category and +0x448 selected item consumed by the command-five handler.
Provides exact initialized building definitions independently of menu availability.
Provides the last accepted initialized wonder definition independently of this UI limit.
Owns the broader meaning and limits of the called wonder gate 0x82CF3608.

ownership.parent: At 0x82E01960 the parent allocates 0x4E4 bytes; 0x82E01970 calls constructor 0x82DFC528 and 0x82E0197C stores its result at parent +0xC40. The constructor stores vtable 0x82125548 at child +0x00 and initializes child +0x434/+0x438/+0x43C to zero and +0x440 through +0x450 to -1. This is distinct from the GFX_CityList.gfx object at 0x82E03528, whose same-numbered offsets cannot be joined to this child by offset alone.
ownership.parentArrays: At 0x82E017F4, 0x82E01804, 0x82E01814, and 0x82E0182C the parent calls four category generators and stores their returned counts at parent +0x438, +0x43C, +0x440, and +0x444. At 0x82E01980 through 0x82E019A0 it passes the selected category count from parent[270+category], its fixed 400-byte category array at parent +0x44C+400*category, category, and city index to 0x82DFF310.
ownership.optionCopy: 0x82DFF310 resets the child vector rooted at +0x430, iterates the supplied count of 32-bit entries, and appends entries greater than -1 for categories 0 through 2. If the resulting vector is empty it sets child +0x08 to one; otherwise it stores category at +0x440 and city index at +0x444. The extra category-four allowance is outside building and wonder choices.
ownership.selection: At 0x82E01620, a parsed option index must be nonnegative and below (child +0x438 - child +0x434)/4. At 0x82E01690 it copies that vector entry into child +0x448; at 0x82E016B4 it stores -1 for an invalid index. The command-five handler later reads this +0x448. This is a vector-index check, not a proof that each entry names an initialized definition.

wonderChoice.generator: Parent setup calls 0x82CE2FD0 at 0x82E01814 with the city index and the parent wonder array at +0x76C. The generator has an early city-state branch: city flags +0x24 bit 0x400 plus current item +0x38 at least 200 returns zero.
wonderChoice.loop: At 0x82CE3034 through 0x82CE3068, the generator walks 33 eight-byte slots from runtime table 0x830E5148 to exclusive end 0x830E5250. It only tests a slot when its first signed word equals -1; it calls 0x82CF3608 with normalized index 0 through 32 and signed city-owner byte, and appends index+200 only when that helper returns nonzero. It returns the appended count.
wonderChoice.bound: This production-choice generator can append only item IDs 200 through 232. Initialized definition IDs 233 through 236 are outside its fixed loop. This is a local UI-enumeration bound, not a global definition-table end or a proof that another path cannot use those IDs.
wonderChoice.state: The 33 loop slots are zero in the pinned image, but wonder-claim-slot-state establishes a 0x108-byte all-FF reset and a mode-one owner/city writer for this mutable table. Its one-city runtime observation found both words at -1 in all 33 slots and nonzero eligibility for indices 2, 8, 11, 12, and 14 through 18. Other menu states and the final option vector were not observed.

buildingChoice.source: At 0x82E017F4 the parent calls 0x82CED7E8 with mode 1 for the unit array; at 0x82E01804 it calls 0x82CED700 with mode 2 for the building array. 0x82CED700 calls the large 0x82CEBC38 city-list generator, copies its output from a 100-word scratch array after leading negative values, and returns the copied count.
buildingChoice.modeAndLoop: 0x82CEBC38 preserves incoming mode 2. At 0x82CEC5D4 it takes the bit-one path; at 0x82CEC644 its clear bit zero skips the unit-output loop. If its building-loop guard is nonzero, the loop at 0x82CEC878 reads live count 0x830E45CC and, after local conditions, appends index+100 at 0x82CECA38 through 0x82CECA40 for indices below that count. The initializer at 0x82D251A0 through 0x82D251AC writes 23 to that count. With that initialized count, this list path can append building IDs 100 through 122 and no higher building ID from this loop.
buildingChoice.qualification: 0x82CEBC38 has city-state, map, technology, and building checks across a large body. The predicates deciding which IDs appear remain unclosed. The count is read from a live global; later indirect mutation and runtime list contents were not observed. The cost helper's broader 100 through 199 range is not a menu-validity rule.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only Ghidra exact-word, reference, function, and bounded raw-store queries against the pinned image. Generated-code corroboration was restricted to the exact parent, constructor, option-copy, selection, and four category-generator functions when Ghidra truncated at save/restore thunks.
currentEvidence.qualification: One city-menu pass observed the mutable 0x830E5148 table and gate returns, but not the final list options. Ghidra decompilation truncates several relevant functions at save/restore thunks; exact raw words and narrow generated-code dataflow corroborate the reported branches.

guards: Do not treat matching object offsets as ownership proof; 0x82E03528 is a different CityList class.
Do not infer that IDs 233 through 236 are absent definitions or globally unusable from this one 33-entry menu loop.
Do not generalize the one observed menu pass to other city states or infer final option-vector contents from this probe.
Do not claim complete building validity from the 100-word scratch capacity, the initialized 23-count, or the initialized record block.
RVA-F-0185.conclusion: The actual production-choice child receives a filtered vector of IDs from category-specific parent arrays and copies an in-range vector entry to the selected-item field read by the command-five handler. The wonder array generator tests exactly normalized indices 0 through 32 and can emit IDs 200 through 232; the runtime sentinel and eligibility result decide which appear. The building path uses mode 2 and a live count initialized to 23, so its indexed append loop yields only IDs 100 through 122 under that initialized count. Building-list predicates, later count mutation, other UI paths, and global validity remain unresolved.

RVA-F-0188.question: Which bounded direct-call sources submit command type five outside the accepted city-choice producer?

scope.callsiteLookback: 0x100 bytes before each exact local-drain and separate-submit call
scope.literalFilter: PowerPC addi rD,r0,5 (li rD,5) raw word
scope.stopCondition: Enumerate direct calls to both targets without truncation at caps 64 and 256 respectively, classify each distinct nearby literal-five site, and stop at the exact helper's direct callers.
scope.boundary: The scan covers direct calls in initialized executable memory and a fixed local lookback. It does not follow indirect calls, values loaded from memory or passed by callers, earlier record construction, or other command routes.

dependencies.use: Owns the accepted UI command-five producer and its direct local-drain branch.
Owns the observed command-five item write at city +0x38.
Defines the remaining non-menu source question for initialized IDs 233 through 236.

directCallCensus.localDrain: The raw direct-call scan found 27 calls to 0x82CE16C8 at cap 64, without truncation.
directCallCensus.separateSubmit: A second exact scan found 100 direct calls to 0x82CE1950 at cap 256, without truncation. Seven 0x100-byte pre-call windows contain li rD,5 at six distinct addresses.
directCallCensus.nearbyLiterals: Across 0x100-byte lookbacks for the 27 drain callsites, three pre-call li rD,5 sites were found: 0x82CD0570 before call 0x82CD0670, 0x82CEE6C0 before call 0x82CEE76C, and 0x82D24E0C before call 0x82D24EA4. A second window also overlapped 0x82CEE6C0 after an earlier call; it is not another pre-call candidate.

candidateClassification.result: The command record at stack +0xA0 receives literal type 2 at 0x82CD05DC. Register r30, initially set to 5 and conditionally changed to 2 or 3, is stored at record +0x08 at 0x82CD05E4. The literal is not the command type on this call path.
This is the already accepted 0x82CEE650 UI producer: literal type 5 is stored to its command record before the local-drain call.

Register r9 receives 5 and is moved to CTR at 0x82D24E44 for the five-word copy loop at 0x82D24E48 through 0x82D24E58. The copied record at stack +0xF0 receives its type from retained r20, initialized to 38 on this loop path; the nearby five is a copy count, not a command type.

separateSubmitCandidate.record: At 0x82CB44C8 the helper sets r3 to literal type 5 before calling 0x82CE1950. Its r6 item argument comes from a preceding branch. On the r7 == -12 branch, 0x82CB4498 adds 200 to r6 after a call to 0x82D038E8; on the other type-five branch, 0x82CB44BC copies r7 to r6 after that helper call. The resulting r6 is not bounded here.
separateSubmitCandidate.caller: Exact direct-call census for 0x82CB42B8 found only 0x82CECC98 and 0x82CECCB8, both within the accepted city-list generator 0x82CEBC38. The first passes r6 loaded from an indexed array; the second passes retained r24. The meanings and live values of those inputs are not established by this packet.
separateSubmitCandidate.otherLiteralSites: At 0x82CBB140, r27=5 flows to a non-type argument before a call with r3=2. At 0x82CD0D1C, r9=5 precedes calls 0x82CD0D7C and 0x82CD0DA0, both with r3=43. At 0x82CF41DC, r8=5 precedes a call with r3=28. At 0x82D2C088, r11=5 precedes a call with r3=17. At 0x82D2C298, r20=5 is copied to r6 before a call with r3=18. These local literals do not set the command type at those calls.
separateSubmitCandidate.runtime: No observation of this helper or its type-five branch was made. The earlier Barracks-selection session logged zero type-five calls at the separate submit entry. A later owner-reported wonder selection logged zero events at the helper's 0x82CECC98 caller.
separateSubmitCandidate.qualification: The static branch establishes another type-five producer, not that any specific item ID, including 233 through 236, reaches it. Local li filtering cannot exclude record types constructed earlier, loaded from memory, or sent indirectly.

cityListOrdinalPath.marker: In 0x82CEBC38, the scan at 0x82CEC5E8 through 0x82CEC618 tests eight-byte wonder slots for first word -1 and a nonzero 0x82CF3608(index, owner) result. Its pointer ends at base +0x108 after 33 positions. The success branch writes a -12 candidate marker at 0x82CEC640.
cityListOrdinalPath.selection: When the first chooser result selects that -12 candidate, a second scan at 0x82CECBFC through 0x82CECC54 traverses the same 33 slots and writes qualifying raw ordinals 0 through 32 into a separate array at 0x82CECC38. The second call to 0x82CE8338 returns a row selector. The caller checks only selector != -1 at 0x82CECC78, then reads the selected ordinal at 0x82CECC94 and passes it as r6 to 0x82CB42B8 at 0x82CECC98.
cityListOrdinalPath.helperPreservation: The intervening 0x82D038E8 call in the helper writes a separate global and does not assign r6 in its bounded 0x82D038E8 through 0x82D0392C body. The -12 branch then adds 200 at 0x82CB4498 before submitting type 5.
cityListOrdinalPath.conditionalRange: If the second chooser returns a valid row of the populated ordinal array, this path submits only IDs 200 through 232. The visible caller checks against -1 but does not check the upper row bound. The known initialized vtable resolves the chooser's indirect slot +0x30 call, but the eventual dialog row-return contract remains unproved. The unconditional reachable ID bound therefore remains unproved.
cityListOrdinalPath.runtime: No invocation of this submit path or second chooser result was observed. One owner-reported wonder selection logged zero events at 0x82CECC98 and cannot establish that the path is unused.

cityListDirectCallers.census: An exact direct-call scan for 0x82CEBC38 found seven sites at cap 16, without truncation: 0x82CB9FEC, 0x82CBA098, 0x82CBA1C8, 0x82CED784, 0x82CED86C, 0x82D160F8, and 0x82D1E0E0.
cityListDirectCallers.modes: The three 0x82CB6E48 AI-turn calls, city-update call 0x82D160F8, and turn-follow-up call 0x82D1E0E0 pass mode -1. The production-choice building-array wrapper 0x82CED700 calls at 0x82CED784 with mode 2; unit-array wrapper 0x82CED7E8 calls at 0x82CED86C with mode 1.
cityListDirectCallers.markerGate: At 0x82CEC5D4 through 0x82CEC5DC, the -12 marker scan requires mode bit 0x2. Modes -1 and 2 can enter that scan; mode 1 skips it. Entry additionally depends on an empty wonder slot and nonzero 0x82CF3608 result. Reaching 0x82CECC98 requires the first chooser to select the -12 candidate and the second chooser to return a value other than -1; the visible caller does not reject other negative values. The ordinary wonder-choice array is generated through a separate 0x82CE2FD0 path; an owner selecting a displayed wonder is not by itself an invocation of this -12 branch.
cityListDirectCallers.qualification: The seven calls exhaust direct calls in initialized executable memory, not indirect calls. Caller mode alone does not prove the local marker, chooser results, or live invocation. The exact user action that selects -12 remains unresolved.

chooserReturnFrontier.knownReceiver: 0x82CE8338 calls receiver 0x8314F76C through slot +0x30 at 0x82CE86F4. The accepted initialized vtable 0x82138768 has 0x82D84630 at word 0x82138798. Other live vptr states are not excluded.
chooserReturnFrontier.returnChain: The known target 0x82D84630 can return -1; its other path calls 0x82E2F1A0 at 0x82D84798. That helper can also return -1 and otherwise forwards the 0x82E07290 result from call 0x82E2F368. The dialog body initializes field +0x42C to -1 at 0x82E072D4 and returns it at 0x82E07810, without a visible direct upper-row test in this chain.
chooserReturnFrontier.constructedObject: Constructor 0x82E056F8 installs vtable 0x8212431C at 0x82E0575C after initializing +0x42C to -1 at 0x82E05730. Its slot +0x34 word 0x82124350 targets 0x82E053E8, which can reset +0x42C to -1 at 0x82E05474. Slot +0x04 word 0x82124320 targets 0x82E07200. Slot +0x30 word 0x8212434C targets the selected-row return writer 0x82E05490.
chooserReturnFrontier.rowSource: 0x82E07290 copies the supplied vector using its preceding count word at 0x82E072F0. One dialog callback 0x82E06C70 parses its r5 string as a base-ten integer at call 0x82E06D50 and passes that result as r4 to 0x82E06B88 at 0x82E06D60. The parser checks digits but does not compare the result with the dialog count. A second direct 0x82E06B88 caller passes constant row zero at 0x82E071C4. At 0x82E06BB0, 0x82E06B88 stores r4 into dialog +0x470 before calling 0x82E06968 at 0x82E06BB8.
chooserReturnFrontier.countAndCommit: On its +0x478 == 0 path, 0x82E06968 rejects negative +0x470 values and values at least the 16-byte-entry count computed from dialog +0x454 and +0x458 at 0x82E06A18 through 0x82E06A40; it also rejects an entry whose first word is -1 at 0x82E06A58. This comparison gates later content handling, not the prior +0x470 store. Constructor 0x82E056F8 initializes +0x478 to zero, but dialog body 0x82E07290 then stores incoming r7 to +0x478 at 0x82E072CC; a nonzero path invokes that callback without the local count comparison. Vtable slot +0x30 target 0x82E05490 checks state bytes +0x11 and +0x434, then copies +0x470 to return field +0x42C at 0x82E05518 through 0x82E0551C without a row-count comparison. 0x82E07290 returns +0x42C at 0x82E07810. The copied vector count and the +0x454/+0x458 entry count are not proved identical in every state.
chooserReturnFrontier.smallestNextObservation: At 0x82CECC98, raw r11 is the second chooser selector times four, r31 is the 33-slot scan ordinal, r30 is the populated-array end, and r15-3808 is its base. The approved default-off pre-instruction observer logged r11, r31, r30, r15, r6 chosen ordinal, r4 first chooser row, and r3 player with an eight-event cap, but one owner-reported wonder selection produced zero events. The next narrower predecessor discriminator is a default-off pre-instruction observation at 0x82CECBD0, capped at eight events, of r27 selected row and r11 selected candidate before comparison with -12. It would distinguish a different first selection from the -12 marker when that first chooser is reached; it was prepared as an address and field specification but not built or run. A future event at 0x82CECC98 would establish a live row and item, not a program-wide valid-ID rule. For the dialog edge, a same-object observation at parser handoff 0x82E06D60 and commit 0x82E0551C could record parsed r4, +0x470, +0x42C, and the +0x454/+0x458 count; no such probe was built or run.

runtimeObservation.method: A temporary default-off scratch Title hook was generated before the guest 0x82CECC98 call, read registers only, and capped logging at eight events. It was enabled by launch argument for one interactive Xenos session using an isolated user-data root whose two input files were copied and hash-checked before launch. ReXGlue codegen and build passed; CTest passed 41 and skipped one. The process exited normally with code zero. The owner reported selecting a wonder. The log contained zero city-list-row events.
runtimeObservation.qualification: The hook was present in generated code before the call and the enabled launch argument was supplied, but no positive hook hit occurred. This single negative does not show whether the -12 marker was available, either chooser selected it, any other call path submitted the selected wonder, or the route is globally unused.

currentEvidence.method: Sequential foreground read-only canonical-project queries enumerated raw direct calls, read 0x100-byte windows around the 27 local-drain and 100 separate-submit callsites, enumerated two helper callers and seven city-list-generator callers, and read exact caller, chooser, vtable, row-store, and count-test words.
